    What is the story behind Guernica?
    Picasso's painting is based on the events of April 27, 1937, when Hitler's powerful German air force, acting in support of Franco, bombed the village of Guernica in northern Spain, a city of no strategic military value. It was history's first aerial saturation bombing of a civilian population.

    Why was Picasso's painting Guernica so controversial?
    In June of 1937, Pablo Picasso created a masterpiece to convey the negative effects of war by recreating a real event. Guernica is a city that the Nazis bombed during the Spanish Civil War. The bombing occurred on April 27, 1937. Nazi forces bombarded Guernica without caring that it held no strategic military value.

    What does the Picasso Guernica symbolize?
    While art critics and historians have different opinions about the symbolism in Guernica, there is general agreement that the painting represents the horror and chaos of war. Many people think of Guernica as an anti-war statement and a prescient warning about the war that would soon engulf the world.

    Description

    Guernica is a large 1937 oil painting by Spanish artist Pablo Picasso. It is one of his best-known works, regarded by many art critics as the most moving and powerful anti-war painting in history. It is exhibited in the Museo Reina Sofía in Madrid. Wikipedia
    Artist: Pablo Picasso
    Locations: Paris (1937–1937), Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía
    Dimensions: 11′ 6″ x 25′ 6″
    Periods: Cubism, Surrealism
    Created: April 26, 1937–June 1937
    Genre: History painting
    Subject: War, Spanish Civil War, Suffering
